ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the medians $AD$ and $BE$ of $\triangle ABC$ intersect each other at point $F$. Through point $E$, draw $EG\parallel AD$ where it intersects $BC$ at point $G$. What is the value of the ratio $EG\colon AF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect DE.\\
AD, BE are the medians of the triangle\\
$\therefore$DE$\parallel$AB, DE=$\frac{1}{2}$AB\\
$\therefore$$\triangle$DEF$\sim$$\triangle$ABF\\
$\therefore$$\frac{DF}{AF}=\frac{DE}{AB}=\frac{1}{2}$\\
$\therefore$AF=$\frac{2}{3}AD$\\
$\because$ED$\parallel$AD\\
$\therefore$$\triangle$EGC$\sim$$\triangle$ADC\\
$\therefore$$\frac{EG}{AD}=\frac{CE}{AC}=\frac{1}{2}$\\
$\therefore$EG=$\frac{1}{2}AD$\\
$\therefore$EG$\colon$AF=$\boxed{\frac{3}{4}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, with BC as the horizontal base, B on the left and C on the right, and A above; D is on BC, and AD is the median from A to BC; E is on AC, and BE is the median from B to AC; AD and BE intersect at F; through E draw a line segment EG parallel to AD, intersecting BC at G. Reasoning: By the coordinate method, take B=(0,0), C=(2,0), then the midpoint of BC is D=(1,0). Let A=(u,v), where v is not 0. Because BE is a median, E is the midpoint of AC, E=((u+2)/2, v/2). The intersection point F of the two medians is the centroid of the triangle, therefore F=((u+2)/3, v/3). Vector AD = D-A = (1-u, -v). Vector AF = F-A = ((u+2)/3-u, v/3-v) = (2/3)(1-u, -v), so the length of AF is 2/3 of the length of AD. Also because EG is parallel to AD, the line through E can be written as E+t(1-u,-v). Its y-coordinate is v/2 - tv; when it intersects BC, y=0, so t=1/2. Therefore the length of EG is 1/2 of the length of AD. Thus EG:AF = (1/2):(2/3)=3/4.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/vector route. From the diagram, take BC as a horizontal base with B=(0,0), C=(2,0), so the midpoint D of BC is D=(1,0). Let A=(u,v). From the text, BE is a median, so E is the midpoint of AC: E=((u+2)/2, v/2). The intersection F of medians is the centroid, or compute it as F=((u+2)/3, v/3). Then vector AD=(1-u,-v), and vector AF=F-A=(2/3)(1-u,-v), so AF=(2/3)AD in length. Since EG is drawn through E parallel to AD and ends on BC, write the line as E+t(1-u,-v). Its y-coordinate is v/2-tv, which becomes 0 at t=1/2. Hence EG=(1/2)AD in length. Therefore EG:AF=(1/2):(2/3)=3/4.

method.method_draft: Centroid-and-midline theorem route. From the figure and text, AD and BE are medians, so D is the midpoint of BC and E is the midpoint of AC. Their intersection F is the centroid of triangle ABC. By the centroid theorem, F divides median AD in the ratio AF:FD=2:1, hence AF=2/3 AD. Now look at triangle ACD. Since E is the midpoint of AC and EG is drawn parallel to AD, the line through midpoint E parallel to side AD meets CD at its midpoint G, and EG is a mid-segment of triangle ACD. Therefore EG=1/2 AD. 推理：题设说明 AD 和 BE 是三角形 ABC 的中线，所以 D 是 BC 的中点，E 是 AC 的中点。两条中线相交于 F，因此 F 是三角形 ABC 的重心。由重心定理，F 将中线 AD 按 AF:FD=2:1 分割，所以 AF=(2/3)AD。

Reasoning: By the coordinate method, take B=(0,0), C=(2,0), then the midpoint of BC is D=(1,0). Let A=(u,v), where v is not 0. Because BE is a median, E is the midpoint of AC, E=((u+2)/2, v/2). The intersection point F of the two medians is the centroid of the triangle, therefore F=((u+2)/3, v/3). Vector AD = D-A = (1-u, -v). Vector AF = F-A = ((u+2)/3-u, v/3-v) = (2/3)(1-u, -v), so the length of AF is 2/3 of the length of AD. Also because EG is parallel to AD, the line through E can be written as E+t(1-u,-v). Its y-coordinate is v/2 - tv; when it intersects BC, y=0, so t=1/2. Therefore the length of EG is 1/2 of the length of AD. Thus EG:AF = (1/2):(2/3)=3/4.
